system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The PowerShell window reported at about 13:40 UTC is consistent with the documented workstation-patching practice: Omar Haddad authenticated to WS-MLOPEZ-01 from WS-OHADDAD-01, then PowerShell ran the specified Deploy-Patches.ps1 script from FILE-HD-01.

The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update, and the proxy recorded a Windows Update Agent connection transferring about 38.8 MB; this supports a patching explanation for the reported window.
Before the reported PowerShell activity, Sysmon recorded csrss.exe accessing lsass.exe with GrantedAccess=0x1400. The record does not establish why this access occurred.

A Cisco AnyConnect vpnagent.exe process started on WS-MLOPEZ-01, and a separate UDP connection from that host to port 1812 was recorded. The logs do not link the connection to that process or show a VPN session.
SMB connections from WS-MLOPEZ-01 to DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 were associated with ANONYMOUS LOGON network logons; the records do not show which shares or resources, if any, were accessed.
Microsoft Defender ran a scan and later created a DetectionHistory file, but the supplied records do not include the detection details or outcome.

known_telemetry_limitations: The process and network records do not provide the contents or integrity of Deploy-Patches.ps1, the downloaded update, or the resulting patch-installation status.
The supplied SMB records show connections and logons but not share names, file operations, or the purpose of the anonymous logons.
The supplied records do not provide details for the Defender DetectionHistory entry.
The logs do not identify the process responsible for the UDP connection to port 1812 or show whether AnyConnect established a VPN session.
claims_not_established: Whether the csrss.exe access to lsass.exe was legitimate or malicious.
Whether AnyConnect or the port 1812 connection represents unauthorized remote access.
Whether the SMB sessions involved unauthorized access or meaningful data transfer.
Whether Defender detected a threat, and, if so, whether it was related to the other activity.
Whether all activity on WS-MLOPEZ-01 during the review window was benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve the Defender detection details and correlate them with the scan and DetectionHistory file.
Review endpoint process, file, and security telemetry around the csrss.exe-to-lsass.exe access, including any related alerts or process integrity information.
Determine the origin and purpose of the UDP port 1812 traffic and whether AnyConnect was configured or used to establish a connection.
Review SMB share and object-access auditing on DC-HD-01 and FILE-HD-01 for the sessions from WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Verify the script and update package against the approved patch deployment, including script contents, signature or hash, and installation results.
